headline: KSE-100 surges 1,841 points to a record 170,885 on broad-based buying, Wall Street closes a volatile Fed-hike week mixed with the 10-year near 5%, and gold clears $4,350 as an IMF mission arrives this week for Pakistan's fourth EFF review
mood: Cautiously constructive · IMF review and the Fed's rate path the swing factors

five_things.html: The KSE-100 surged 1,841.39 points (+1.09%) on Friday to close at a record 170,884.58, extending Thursday's rebound as buying swept automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, exploration & production and OMCs; index heavyweights LUCK, MCB, MEBL, NBP, UBL, MARI, OGDC, POL, PPL and PSO all traded in the green. Breadth was decisively positive — 351 of 496 traded names advanced versus 110 declines — on turnover of roughly 165.8 million KSE-100 shares, with Media Times, WorldCall Telecom and Cnergyico topping the volume table. Business Recorder and Daily Independent confirm the print.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Ends Fed-Hike Week Mixed
five_things.html: US equities closed a volatile week quietly: the S&P 500 edged up 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq gained 0.39% to 26,522.55, while the Dow slipped 0.18% to 51,682.64 — its third straight losing week and worst since March. The move came as traders digested Wednesday's first Fed rate hike in three years and priced rising odds of a follow-up increase at the October 28 meeting. TheStreet and BBN Times.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.01%, its highest level of the run-up, while the 2-year holds near 4.75%, as markets moved to price a roughly 58% chance of another 25bp increase at the Fed's October 28 meeting after 16 of 18 officials' dot-plot projections showed room for at least one more hike this year. Yahoo Finance and CNBC.

Brent eased to $103.87/bbl (−0.91%) and WTI fell 1.6% to $100.30, extending the week's pullback as Saudi Arabia's drone-damaged East-West pipeline nears full repair; both benchmarks remain well above pre-attack levels. Separately, OPEC+ confirmed it will pause its monthly output increases for October, holding the group's target at 31.1 million bpd with the next review set for October 4. CNBC. A softer barrel remains a tailwind for Pakistan's import bill even as OPEC+ signals no further easing near-term.

Gold climbed 0.60% to about $4,368.60/oz, touching a weekly high near $4,440, while silver jumped 3.02% to $67.18, extending the post-Fed rally for a second straight session as easing oil dragged yields off their highs and compressed the gold/silver ratio to roughly 65 — its tightest of the week. In Washington, Congress's stopgap funding law signed September 2 keeps the government open only through December 11, setting up the next fiscal cliff just as the Fed weighs an October hike. USAGOLD and NPR.

matrix.local_html: Friday's 1.09% PSX rally to a record 170,884.58 capped a strong week as banks, autos, cement and E&P led broad-based buying, with breadth firmly positive (351 advancers vs. 110 decliners) on roughly 165.8 million KSE-100 shares traded. The State Bank held its policy rate at 11.5% at its September 14 MPC meeting even as August CPI printed at 11.1% y/y (urban 10.4%, rural 12.2%) — up from 9.2% in July — per Business Recorder; 6-month KIBOR sits near 11.98% per SBP. The rupee held steady at 277.25 interbank, per Business Recorder. An IMF mission is due in Islamabad around September 22-23 for the fourth EFF review, third RSF review and the first Article IV consultation in two years; Pakistan has reportedly met six of seven end-June performance targets, with tax-net broadening the lone laggard, per PhotoNews Pakistan.
matrix.gcc_html: Oil eased further to close the week — Brent at $103.87 and WTI at $100.30 — as Saudi Arabia's damaged East-West pipeline nears full repair, per CNBC. OPEC+ confirmed it will pause its monthly output increases for October, holding the group's combined target at 31.1 million bpd after months of steady restoration, with the next review set for October 4. Non-oil momentum stays firm — Saudi Arabia's PMI held at a six-month high of 53.8 in August, per Arab News, while the UAE's composite reading climbed to 55.3, its strongest since late 2024, per The National.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street closed a volatile, Fed-dominated week on a quiet note: the S&P 500 edged up 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq rose 0.39% to 26,522.55, while the Dow slipped 0.18% to 51,682.64 for its third straight losing week, per TheStreet. The 10-year Treasury climbed to about 5.01% as markets priced a roughly 58% chance of another 25bp hike at the Fed's October 28 meeting, following Wednesday's first increase in three years to 3.75%-4.00%, per Yahoo Finance. Separately, Congress's stopgap funding law signed September 2 keeps federal agencies funded only through December 11, setting up the next shutdown cliff.

legislative.impact_html: Wins: Gulf producers defending price levels ahead of 2027 budget planning Loses: oil-importing economies in Asia facing a firmer crude floor than a resumed-hike scenario would have delivered

legislative.impact_html: Wins: the dollar and short-duration savers on a still-tightening path Loses: long-duration bonds and rate-sensitive growth names pricing a higher terminal rate, plus agencies facing another funding cliff in December

levels.support_note: Friday's intraday low; deeper support at Thursday's 168,223 low

desk_stance_html: We read Friday's 1,841-point rally as continuation rather than exhaustion — breadth was decisively positive and the advance was broad across banks, autos, cement and E&P rather than concentrated in a handful of names. The swing factor into the new week is binary: the IMF mission's arrival around September 22-23 for the fourth EFF and third RSF reviews, with six of seven end-June targets already reportedly met. We would look for a clean break above 171,037 to open a run at 172,000, while a close back below 169,400 would flag that momentum is fading ahead of the IMF verdict. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

linkedin_text:
KSE-100 surges 1,841 points to a record 170,885 on broad-based buying — while Wall Street closes a volatile Fed-hike week mixed and gold clears $4,350 ahead of Pakistan's IMF review.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US equities closed a volatile week quietly: the S&P 500 edged up 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq gained 0.39% to 26,522.55, while the Dow slipped 0.18% to 51,682.64 — its third straight losing week and worst since March. The 10-year Treasury climbed to about 5.01% as markets priced a roughly 58% chance of another 25bp Fed hike at the October 28 meeting, following Wednesday's first increase in three years to 3.75%-4.00%.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 gained 1,841.39 points (+1.09%) on Friday to close at a record 170,884.58, with breadth decisively positive — 351 advancers versus 110 decliners — on roughly 165.8 million KSE-100 shares traded. Automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, exploration & production and OMCs led, with LUCK, MCB, MEBL, NBP, UBL, MARI, OGDC, POL, PPL and PSO all in the green. The State Bank held its policy rate at 11.5% at its September 14 meeting despite August CPI at 11.1% y/y; 6-month KIBOR sits near 11.98%. The rupee held steady near 277.25 interbank. An IMF mission is due in Islamabad around September 22-23 for the fourth EFF review, third RSF review and the first Article IV consultation in two years; Pakistan has reportedly met six of seven end-June performance targets, with tax-net broadening the lone laggard.

GCC
Brent eased to $103.87 (−0.91%) and WTI fell 1.6% to $100.30, extending the week's pullback as Saudi Arabia's damaged East-West pipeline nears full repair. OPEC+ confirmed it will pause its monthly output increases for October, holding the group's combined target at 31.1 million bpd, with the next review set for October 4. Non-oil momentum stays firm — Saudi PMI held at a six-month high of 53.8, UAE's composite reading climbed to 55.3, its strongest since late 2024.

GLOBAL
Gold climbed 0.60% to about $4,368.60/oz, touching a weekly high near $4,440, while silver jumped 3.02% to $67.18, extending the post-Fed rally as easing oil dragged yields off their highs. In Washington, Congress's stopgap funding law signed September 2 keeps the government open only through December 11, setting up the next fiscal cliff just as the Fed weighs an October hike.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: IMF's 4th EFF/3rd RSF review + first Article IV consultation (~Sep 22-23) — wins for banks/sovereign credit on a ~$1bn disbursement path; loses for tax-exposed sectors facing fresh scrutiny on the stalled tax-net benchmark.
• GCC: OPEC+ pauses October output increase, holding at 31.1m bpd — wins for Gulf producers defending price levels; loses for oil-importing economies in Asia.
• Global: Fed's Oct 28 meeting carries ~58% hike odds as Congress's CR funds government only through Dec 11 — wins for the dollar and short-duration savers; loses for long-duration bonds and rate-sensitive growth names.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 169,400 (Friday's intraday low) · pivot 170,885 (Friday's close) · resistance 171,037 (Friday's intraday high). We'd look for a clean break above resistance to open a run at 172,000, while a close back below support would flag that momentum is fading ahead of the IMF verdict. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
